summary: Trap: 130-160 BPM felt half-time, TR-808 drums with rolling 16th/32nd/triplet hats and a snare or clap on 3, a long sub 808 bass as the loudest thing, dark minor chords and a sparse bell melody; knowledge/style/trap.json is its template
body: Tempo 130-160 BPM (140 is a good start; some go up to 200), felt half-time: the snare lands on 3, so it reads as 65-80.

Drums: TR-808 sounds. A punchy kick, syncopated and lining up with the 808 bass; snare and clap together on 3; closed hats in straight 16ths with 32nd and 1/6 or 1/12 triplet rolls (the middle hits softer), changing every couple of bars; an open hat now and then. Straight, not swung; little reverb on the drums.
Bass: the 808, a long sub boom (decay well past 300 ms) on the roots in E1-E2, following the kick, with gaps; semitone moves sound sinister. It is the loudest thing.
Harmony: minor, two to four chords (i-VI, i-VI-iv-v), dark, held low on strings, a choir or a pad.
Lead: a short, sparse, dark melody on bells (celesta, glockenspiel), plucks, piano or flute, with more reverb than the drums.
Texture/master: sparse, punchy and weighty, loud; the sub carries on big systems and the 808's harmonics on phones; light saturation on drums, a clean top.

Sources (2026-11-26): Native Instruments 'How to make a trap beat'; Mode Audio 'Trap: 5 Production Essentials'; MusicRadar 'The beginner's guide to: trap' and '10 tricks every trap producer should know'; EDMProd 'How To Make Trap Music'.

Apply: pattern/trap-halftime on the drums, then pattern/prog-trap-characteristic-1 on the keys four bars later. For a whole style change the Team Lead's restyle uses knowledge/style/trap.json instead.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
